winnerSummary: Debt relief ads with the longest run durations share three patterns: (1) **Specific numbers everywhere** — exact debt amounts ($47k, $83k), settlement ratios (25 cents on the dollar, 50% reduction), and timelines (27 months, 90 seconds to qualify). Vague promises don't run long; specificity does. (2) **Fear + relief in one breath** — the best-performing hooks agitate the fear (drowning in interest, stuck on minimums) then immediately imply effortless escape (one phone call, 2-minute check). The tension-release cycle drives clicks. (3) **Legal and authority framing** dominates over personal testimonials — 'government program', 'legally required', 'bankruptcy attorney says' all outperform pure UGC in this vertical because trust is the primary objection. The winning angle gap is **proactive pre-crisis targeting** (the 'warning signs' format) rather than waiting for the audience to be in full panic mode.
